stem: The properties of elements and their compounds show similarities, differences and trends depending on the positions of the elements in the Periodic Table.

parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.text: the element that forms an amphoteric oxide,

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.text: the element with the highest first ionisation energy,

parts.label: (a)(iii)
parts.text: the element that forms a soluble hydroxide and an insoluble sulfate,

parts.label: (a)(iv)
parts.text: the most volatile element in a group that contains elements in all three states of matter at room temperature and pressure,

parts.label: (a)(v)
parts.text: the element that forms the largest cation.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.stem: The elements in Group 2 all react with oxygen and with water.
parts.text: State and explain the conditions needed for magnesium to react with oxygen.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text: State what would be seen during the reaction in (b)(i).

parts.label: (b)(iii)
parts.text: Write an equation for the reaction of magnesium with cold water. Include state symbols.

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.stem: The carbonates and nitrates of the elements in Group 2 can all be decomposed by heating.
parts.text: Write an equation for the thermal decomposition of magnesium nitrate.

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text:
The thermal decomposition of calcium carbonate forms a solid product that is industrially important. This solid product reacts with water to form a compound commonly known as slaked lime.

Write equations for the thermal decomposition of calcium carbonate and the reaction of the solid product to form slaked lime.

parts.label: (d)(i)
parts.stem: Calcium carbonate and calcium hydroxide both have an important use in agriculture.
parts.text: Describe this use and explain what makes these two compounds suitable for it.

parts.label: (d)(ii)
parts.text: Write an ionic equation to illustrate this use of calcium carbonate.
